Home — Building Applications with AI Agents

Poori book, Hinglish me — 13 chapters, agent systems ko design karne se lekar production me monitor aur protect karne tak.

  • 85 sections — har chapter ka intro + uske core topics, sab Hinglish me, har section ke end me Source line ke saath.
  • 36 book figures — book ke diagrams, captions ke saath, isi file ke andar.
  • 49 code blocks — book me chhapa code poora, aur companion repo ki har file ka GitHub link.
  • 8 interactive labs — haath se try karo: autonomy slider, tool selection, RAG, Reflexion loop, multi-agent patterns, eval scoring, aur zyada.
  • Interview ki taiyaari ke liye end me 36 FAQs hain, aur Trust Check me is SPA ki coverage ka live hisaab hai.

Ye book agent systems ke poore lifecycle ko cover karti hai — concept se lekar deployment aur maintenance tak. Pehle 3 chapters core concepts, design principles aur UX dete hain; agle 5 chapters agents ko banana, orchestrate karna aur scale karna sikhate hain; aakhri 5 chapters validation, monitoring, security, improvement aur human-agent collaboration par hain. Book modular hai — jis section se chaaho, wahin se shuru kar sakte ho.

Yaad rakhne wala formula

Agent = foundation model + tools + memory + planning + orchestration — aur in sab ko measurement, monitoring aur protection se bandhna padta hai, tabhi woh production me bharosemand banta hai.

01Part 1 — Core Concepts

Chapter 1 — Introduction to Agents

Autonomous agent ek aisa intelligent system hai jo independently data analyse karta hai, apne environment ko interpret karta hai, aur context ke hisaab se decisions leta hai. Is chapter me foundation samjho — asli agent kya hota hai, pretraining revolution ne kya badla, agent ke 7 types, model selection, kab agent mat banao, aur effective agentic systems ke 5 principles.

Book ka key test ye hai: kya system me real decision making hai, ya woh sirf static scripts / deterministic steps follow kar raha hai? Agar sirf fixed script chal rahi hai, to woh asli agent nahi hai — naam me "agent" likhne se agent nahi ban jaata.

Book "agentic system" ka matlab batata hai: tools + memory + foundation model + orchestration + supporting infrastructure, sab milke. Foundation models ab sirf human-readable text nahi, structured function signatures aur parameter selections bhi generate kar sakte hain — orchestration framework phir un functions ko execute karta hai (data lookup, external system ko manipulate karna, concrete actions lena).

Chapter ka core idea

"Agent" term popular hote hi dilute ho gaya hai — bahut si cheezein agent kehlati hain jinme genuine autonomy hoti hi nahi. Pehle ye decide karo ki tumhe agent chahiye bhi ya nahi — phir sahi type, sahi model, aur sahi principles chuno.

01.1Chapter 1 — Introduction to Agents

Asli Agent Kya Hota Hai

Autonomous agent ek aisa intelligent system hai jo independently data analyse karta hai, apne environment ko interpret karta hai, aur context ke hisaab se decisions leta hai. Book ka key test ye hai: kya system me real decision making hai, ya woh sirf static scripts / deterministic steps follow kar raha hai?

Kaise kaam karta hai: foundation models ab sirf human-readable text nahi, structured function signatures aur parameter selections bhi generate kar sakte hain. Orchestration framework phir un functions ko execute karta hai — data lookup, external system ko manipulate karna, concrete actions lena. Book is poori supporting functionality ko "agentic system" kehta hai: tools + memory + foundation model + orchestration + supporting infrastructure, sab milke.

Kyun matter karta hai: "Agent" term popular hote hi dilute ho gaya hai — bahut si cheezein agent kehlati hain jinme genuine autonomy hoti hi nahi. Genuinely autonomous, adaptive agent design karna challenging hai, isiliye bahut si teams jaldi result ke liye simpler approach le leti hain. Isiliye pehle ye decide karna zaroori hai ki tumhe agent chahiye bhi ya nahi.

Example: protocols jaise Model Context Protocol (Chapter 4 me) aur Agent-to-Agent Protocol (Chapter 8 me) agents ko remote tools use karne aur doosre agents ke saath collaborate karne dete hain — isse sophisticated automation ke bade opportunities khulte hain, lekin saath me responsibility bhi aati hai ki systems ko thoughtfully design, measure, aur manage kiya jaaye taaki unke actions human values se align karein aur complex, dynamic environments me safely operate karein.

01.2Chapter 1 — Introduction to Agents

Pretraining Revolution

Traditional ML me practitioner ka zyada time model train karne me nahi, dataset collect aur clean karne me jaata tha, aur performance dataset ki quantity/quality se limited thi. Pretrained generative models ne ye practice ulta di: ek hi model bina extra training ke bahut saare tasks me adapt kar sakta hai.

Kaise kaam karta hai: large volumes of data par trained generative models ab single hosted-model call se available hain — bina training ya hosting ke. LLMs jaise GPT-5, Anthropic's Claude, Meta's Llama, Google's Gemini Ultra, aur DeepSeek's V3 ne difficult tasks par performance aur badha di hai, jisse pretrained models se solve hone wale problems ka scope widen ho gaya hai.

Kyun matter karta hai: isse ML/AI-enabled application banana dramatically sasta aur simple ho gaya hai. Book foundation models ki capabilities list karta hai: natural language understanding, context-aware interaction (lambi interaction me context maintain karna), structured content generation (text, code, structured outputs), contextual interpretation and decision making, tool use, adaptive planning (complex multistep actions autonomously plan aur execute karna), information summarization, unstructured data ka management (emails, documents, logs, reports), code generation (code likhna, execute karna, unit tests likhna), routine task automation, aur multimodal information synthesis (image, audio, video ka analysis at scale).

Example: pehle ML application banane ke liye ML engineer/data scientist hire karo, data collect karo, phir model deploy karo — ab high-quality models ek hosted call se reasonably well kaam kar jaate hain bahut se use cases ke liye, bina training/hosting ke.

01.3Chapter 1 — Introduction to Agents

Agent Ke 7 Types (+ Voice aur Video)

Book agents ko 7 practical types me baantta hai, plus voice aur video agents jo aane wale saalon me adoption badhne ki ummeed hai. Book ka focus language models par built agents par hai, khaas taur par text aur code wale.

  • Business-task agents — predefined business workflows automate karte hain, jaise UiPath's robotic process automation, Microsoft Power Automate's low-code flows, ya Zapier's app integrations; deterministic actions, event-triggered, minimal contextual reasoning.
  • Conversational agents — chatbots/customer service agents, dialogue management, intent recognition, conversational turn-taking.
  • Research agents — information gathering, synthesis, summarization; documents/knowledge bases/web scan karte hain; examples Perplexity AI aur Elicit.
  • Analytics agents — structured datasets interpret karke insights, dashboards, reports; examples Power BI Copilot ya Glean; enterprise data warehouses se tightly integrate.
  • Developer agents — Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot; code generate, refactor, explain karte hain, IDE workflows me deeply integrate.
  • Domain-specific agents — legal (Harvey), medical (Hippocratic AI), finance; domain knowledge + structured workflows.
  • Browser-using agents — websites par navigate, interact, information extract, actions lete hain bina human interaction ke; traditional RPA ke opposite, ye language understanding + visual perception + dynamic planning combine karte hain aur on the fly adapt karte hain.

Voice agents — end-to-end speech understanding aur generation se customer service, appointment scheduling, real-time order processing me conversational automation. Video agents — avatar-based video responses, lip-synced speech, facial expression, gesture; sales, training, customer onboarding, marketing, virtual presence me emerging.

Kyun matter karta hai: term broaden ho gaya hai, isiliye confusion hai ki asli AI agent kya hai. Type pehchanne se ye clear hota hai ki kis problem ke liye kis tarah ka agent chahiye.

01.4Chapter 1 — Introduction to Agents

Model Selection

Model choose karna ek complex aur rapidly changing decision hai — task complexity, modality support, latency aur cost constraints, aur integration requirements ko balance karna padta hai. Book ka reasonable starting point: latest general-purpose model from a leading provider (OpenAI ya Anthropic) se start karo — woh out of the box strong performance deta hai, little customization chahiye, aur bahut se applications me surprisingly far le jaata hai.

Table 1-1 (HELM Core Scenario leaderboard, August 2025) top-10 models ko compare karta hai benchmarks MMLU-Pro, GPQA, IFEval, WildBench, aur Omni-MATH par. Mean scores (exact): GPT-5 mini 0.819; o4-mini 0.812; o3 0.811; GPT-5 0.807; Qwen3 235B A22B Instruct 2507 FP8 0.798; Grok 4 0.785; Claude 4 Opus 0.780; gpt-oss-120b 0.770; Kimi K2 Instruct 0.768; Claude 4 Sonnet 0.766. GPT-5 mini overall lead karta hai highest mean score 0.819 ke saath. Proprietary aur open-access models jaise Qwen3, Grok 4, Claude 4, aur Kimi K2 bhi competitive results dikhate hain.

Lekin chhote models bhi — distillation, quantization, synthetic data generation ki wajah se — bade models se surprising capability inherit kar rahe hain. Trend hai automated model selection: simple queries fast, saste chhote models ko route karo; complex reasoning bade, expensive models ke liye reserve rakho. Ye dynamic test-time optimization effective prove ho rahi hai.

Kyun matter karta hai: model selection par enormous effort karke marginal gains ke peeche bhaagna waste ho sakta hai — jab tak scale ya constraints demand na karein, simple se start karna fine hai. Future almost certainly multimodel hai, isiliye flexibility ke liye design karna aage payoff dega. Over time chhote models try karna, fine-tuning, ya retrieval add karna performance badha aur cost ghata sakta hai.

01.5Chapter 1 — Introduction to Agents

Kab Agent Mat Banao

Ye chapter ka sabse practical section hai: simple script, deterministic workflow, traditional chatbot, RAG system, ya full autonomous agent — galat choice elegant solution aur overengineered, hard-to-maintain mess ka difference ban sakti hai. Chaar key factors: inputs ki variability, reasoning ki complexity, performance/compliance constraints, aur ongoing maintenance burden.

  • Plain code — agar inputs fully predictable hain aur har possible output pehle se describe kiya ja sakta hai, to kuch lines procedural code faster, cheaper, aur test karne me easier hai; millisecond-level latency (embedded system, sensor data) ya regulated domains (medical devices, aeronautics, certain financial systems) jinme fully deterministic, auditable logic chahiye, wahan bhi code hi sahi hai. Example: log file jiska format hamesha "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS—message" ho, use small regex-based parser (Python ya Go) reliably handle kar lega.
  • Deterministic/semiautomated workflow — logic finite steps/branches me express ho sakti hai, human intervention ya error handling ki jagah pehle se pata hai; example: invoices teen known formats (CSV, JSON, PDF) me aati hain — har format ko uske parser par route karo, mismatch check karo, reconciliation fail ho to human review ke liye halt karo; retry with exponential backoff ya manager approval ke liye workflow engine (Airflow, AWS Step Functions) LLM se clearer control deta hai.
  • Traditional chatbot / RAG — natural language understanding + document retrieval, lekin autonomous multistep planning nahi; example: internal IT help desk RAG se "How do I reset my VPN credentials?" ka answer latest troubleshooting guide fetch karke summarize kare; woh ticket file ya callback schedule nahi karta.
  • Autonomous agent — inputs unstructured, novel, highly variable hain aur dynamic multistep planning ya feedback se continuous learning chahiye; example: customer support center jahan free-form emails aati hain "my laptop battery is swelling and might erupt" se "I keep getting billed for services I didn't order" tak — rule-based workflow ya RAG FAQ lookup is variety me toot jaayega, lekin foundation-model agent intent parse karega, entities extract karega, knowledge base consult karega, response draft karega, aur zaroorat ho to human ko escalate karega, bina har branch pehle se bataye.

Table 1-2 (exact rows): Input structure — fully predictable schemas (code) / mostly predictable with finite branches (workflow) / highly unstructured or novel inputs (agent). Explainability — full transparency, easily auditable / explicit branch-by-branch audit trail / black-box components requiring additional tooling. Latency — ultra-low / moderate / higher. Adaptability and learning — none / limited / high (learning from feedback).

Book ke 5 sawaal choose karne se pehle poochho: kya mere inputs unstructured/unpredictable hain? Kya mujhe multistep planning chahiye jo intermediate results se adapt kare? Kya document retrieval kaafi hai ya system ko decide aur act autonomously karna hai? Kya system time ke saath khud improve hona chahiye? Kya main foundation model ki latency aur maintenance burden tolerate kar sakta hoon?

Example: supply chain me agent real-time inventory data, supplier lead times, aur sales forecasts ingest karke shipment schedules dynamically replan kar sakta hai; deterministic workflow ko naye exceptions handle karne ke liye constant manual updates chahiye hote. Security operations agent parallel me threat intelligence APIs query kar sakta hai, network telemetry scan kar sakta hai, aur suspicious binaries par sandbox analysis kar sakta hai.

01.6Chapter 1 — Introduction to Agents

5 Principles aur Frameworks

Effective agentic systems ke liye 5 principles hain — matlab ye 5 baatein yaad rakhna zaroori hai:

  • Scalability — distributed architectures, cloud infrastructure, efficient algorithms, parallel processing; jaise customer support agent jo 10 tickets per minute process karta hai, aur traffic 1,000 par spike ho to autoscaling infrastructure ke bina crash ya hang ho sakta hai.
  • Modularity — independent, interchangeable components, clear interfaces; jaise agent jo saare tools apni agent service me hardcode kar de, to usko chhoti si tool addition ya modification ke liye full redeployment chahiye hoga.
  • Continuous learning — in-context learning jaise mechanisms, user feedback integrate karo; jo agents feedback loops ignore karte hain, woh wahi mistakes baar baar repeat karte hain — jaise contract clauses misclassify karna, ya critical support issues escalate na karna.
  • Resilience — errors, security threats, timeouts, unexpected conditions gracefully handle karo; retry ya fallback logic ke bina agent single API call fail hote hi crash kar sakta hai.
  • Future-proofing — open standards aur scalable infrastructure; ek proprietary vendor ke prompt format se tightly couple hone par model switch karna painful ho jaata hai.

Organization ke liye: pehle exploration encourage karo, phir "one standard per large group" se alignment laao, vendor lock-in avoid karo (OpenAPI jaise open standards), knowledge sharing karo, aur lightweight governance rakho. Premature standardization creativity ko stifle kar sakti hai aur rigid frameworks ya vendor solutions me trap kar sakti hai — isliye exploration aur standardization ka balance iterative hai, matlab ye kaam baar baar hota rehta hai, ek baar me khatam nahi hota.

Frameworks (book ke "Best for" ke saath):

  • LangGraph — modular orchestration, directed graphs, nodes = discrete units of logic (often foundation model calls), edges data flow manage karte hain complex, potentially cyclic workflows ke through; strong developer ergonomics; native async workflows and retries. Trade-off: advanced planning aur memory ke liye custom logic chahiye; built-in multiagent collaboration kam hai. Best for: robust single-agent ya light multiagent systems with explicit, inspectable flow control. Book primarily LangGraph par focus karta hai.
  • AutoGen — powerful multiagent orchestration; dynamic role assignment; flexible messaging-based interaction. Trade-off: simple use cases ke liye heavyweight aur complex hai; agent interaction patterns ke baare me opinionated hai. Best for: research aur production systems involving dialogue between multiple agents (jaise manager-worker, self-reflection loops).
  • CrewAI — easy to learn aur use karna; prototyping ke liye quick setup; abstractions "crew" aur "tasks". Trade-off: orchestration internals par limited customization aur control hai; complex workflows ke liye LangGraph ya AutoGen se less mature hai. Best for: developers jo practical, human-centric agents jaise assistants ya support agents par jaldi start karna chahte hain.
  • OpenAI Agents SDK — OpenAI's tool ecosystem ke saath deep integration; secure, easy-to-use function calling, memory primitives, tool routing. Trade-off: OpenAI infrastructure se tightly coupled hai; custom stacks ya open source toolchains ke liye less flexible aur portable hai. Best for: teams jo pehle se OpenAI API use kar rahi hain, secure, tool-using agents jaldi build karne ka fast way, minimal scaffolding ke saath.

Frameworks necessary nahi hain — bahut si teams seedha model provider APIs par build karti hain. Early prototypes ke liye CrewAI ya OpenAI Agents SDK jaldi start kara dete hain; scalable, production-grade systems ke liye LangGraph aur AutoGen zyada control aur sophistication dete hain.

02Part 1 — Core Concepts

Chapter 2 — Designing Agent Systems

Most practitioners grand design document se start nahi karte — messy problem, foundation model API key, aur rough idea se start karte hain. Ye chapter quick start hai: pehla agent kaise banao, core components kya hain, design trade-offs, single-agent vs multiagent, aur best practices.

Grounding example poore chapter me: ecommerce platform ke liye customer support (order cancel karna). Book ka mantra: "an untested agent is an untrusted agent" — evaluation ke bina agent run to karega, lekin pata nahi chalega ki kitna achha perform kar raha hai.

Chapter ka conclusion: achha agent system start karne ke liye 30-page plan ki zaroorat nahi — lekin thodi foresight bahut kaam aati hai. Tractable slice chunna (jaise canceling orders) se kuch chhota, testable, immediately useful banta hai. Define karo success kya dikhta hai, vague ya over-scoped ambitions avoid karo, clear value jaldi deliver karne par focus karo.

Chapter ka core idea

Effective agent systems parts ka sum se zyada hote hain — strong architecture, disciplined engineering, tight feedback loops par depend karte hain. Iterative development aur robust evaluation se agents time ke saath improve hote hain.

02.1Chapter 2 — Designing Agent Systems

Pehla Agent — Chhota, Bounded Slice

Book ka pehla agent ek narrow, valuable slice par banta hai: customer ka raw message + order record lo, decide karo kaunsa tool call karna hai (issue_refund, cancel_order, ya update_address_for_order), sahi parameters ke saath tool invoke karo, phir brief confirmation message bhejo. Ye two-step workflow narrow enough hai ki jaldi build ho jaaye, valuable enough hai ki human time free kare, aur rich enough hai ki intelligent behaviour showcase kare.

Kaise kaam karta hai: har din support team ko dozens/hundreds emails aate hain — broken mug refund, unshipped order cancel, delivery address change. Human ko free-form text padhna, backend me order lookup karna, appropriate API call karna, phir confirmation email type karna padta hai — ye repetitive two-minute process hai. Agent isey automate karta hai: LangChain @tool se cancel_order(order_id) define karo, phir LLM ko do baar invoke karo — pehli baar tool call decide karne ke liye, tool run karke doosri baar final confirmation text generate karne ke liye — aur LangGraph StateGraph me wire karo (code section me poora code hai).

Scoping balancing act hai: too narrow (sirf cancellations) — refunds ya address changes jaise high-volume requests miss ho jaayenge, real-world impact limited. Too broad ("automate every support inquiry") — billing disputes, product recommendations, technical troubleshooting jaise edge cases me doob jaoge. Too vague ("improve customer satisfaction") — kab succeed hue, pata hi nahi chalega. Clear bounded workflow se concrete inputs (customer message + order record), structured outputs (tool calls + confirmations), aur tight feedback loop milta hai.

Example: email: "Please cancel my order #B73973 because I found a cheaper option elsewhere." Human order lookup karta, verify karta ki ship nahi hua, "Cancel" click karta, confirmation reply karta. Code me ye cancel_order(order_id="B73973") invoke karna + simple confirmation bhejna hai. Example order ID code me A12345 hai; message "Please cancel my order A12345."

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaChapter 2 — Designing Agent SystemsAgla →Core Components — Model, Tools, Memory, Orchestration
02.2Chapter 2 — Designing Agent Systems

Core Components — Model, Tools, Memory, Orchestration

Effective agent system ke core components hain: foundation model (decision-making ka heart), tools (actions karne ki capabilities), memory (context store/retrieve karke seekhna), aur orchestration (isolated capabilities ko end-to-end solution me compose/schedule/supervise karna). Figure 2-1 inhi core components ko dikhata hai.

Model selection: task complexity dekho — large foundation models (GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1) open-ended environments ke liye (nuanced understanding, flexible reasoning, creative generation) lekin zyada compute, cloud infrastructure, higher latency. Smaller models (distilled ModernBERT variants, Phi-4) well-defined repetitive tasks ke liye — local hardware par efficiently chalte hain, fast, saste; customer support, information retrieval, data labeling me achhe. Modality bhi matter karti hai: multimodal models (GPT-5, Claude 4.1) text + images + audio + structured data combine kar sakte hain (healthcare, robotics, customer support); text-only models purely language use cases me lower complexity aur faster inference dete hain. Openness: open source (Llama, DeepSeek) transparency + fine-tune/modify + private hosting, lekin zyada engineering overhead; proprietary (GPT-5, Claude, Cohere) API + managed infrastructure, rapid development, lekin customization limited aur usage ke saath cost scale hoti hai.

Tools teen categories me (Ch 2 me short, Ch 4 me detail): local tools, API-based tools, MCP-based tools. Memory do types: short-term (current task/conversation, rolling context windows) aur long-term (databases, knowledge graphs, ya fine-tuned models; user preferences, historical performance metrics). Orchestration possible tool/skill sequences evaluate karta hai, likely outcomes forecast karta hai, sabse likely-to-succeed path pick karta hai, aur progress/environment monitor karke pause/reroute karta hai.

Kyun matter karta hai: components akele kaam nahi karte — bina solid orchestration layer ke powerful skills bhi cross-purposes par chal sakti hain ya stall ho sakti hain. Model selection one-time decision nahi hai — capabilities, user needs, infrastructure evolve hote hi revisit karni padti hai.

Example: ecommerce support agent ke liye small fast model suffices — lekin agar product recommendations ya sentiment-based escalation add kar do, to larger model nayi capabilities unlock kar sakta hai. Healthcare monitoring agent long-term me patient ke vital signs retain karke trends detect kar sakta hai. Conversational assistant har subtask ka outcome confirm karke phir next plan karta hai, dynamically adapt karte hue.

02.3Chapter 2 — Designing Agent Systems

Design Trade-Offs — Speed, Scalability, Reliability, Cost

Agent design me multiple trade-offs balance karne padte hain: performance (speed/accuracy), scalability (khaas taur par GPU resources), reliability (robust, consistent behaviour), aur costs (development + operational). Kisi ek ko prioritize karoge to doosra sacrifice hoga.

Speed vs accuracy: real-time environments (autonomous vehicles, trading systems) me milliseconds matter karte hain, wahan speed ko accuracy par prioritize karna pad sakta hai; legal analysis ya medical diagnostics me high precision chahiye, wahan speed sacrifice karna acceptable hai. Hybrid approach bhi hai: pehle fast approximate response, phir accurate follow-up se refine karo (recommendation systems, diagnostics me common).

Scalability: GPUs sabse expensive aur limiting factor hain — dynamic GPU allocation (real-time demand par assign karo, idle time ghatao), elastic GPU provisioning (cloud/on-prem GPU clusters jo workload par auto-scale karein), priority queuing aur intelligent task scheduling, asynchronous task execution, dynamic load balancing across GPUs, horizontal scaling (zyada GPU nodes add karo), hybrid cloud + burst scaling (peak par temporary cloud GPUs, demand ghatne par release karo), off-peak hours me cloud GPU instances use karna (demand kam, pricing favourable). Book saaf kehta hai — sirf GPUs add karne se scaling nahi hoti; resources fully utilized hon aur system efficiently scale kare, iske liye careful optimization chahiye.

Reliability: fault tolerance (failures detect karke gracefully recover karo; redundancy — critical components duplicate karo), consistency/robustness (ideal conditions ke saath edge cases, stress tests, real-world constraints me bhi perform kare), extensive testing (unit, integration, real-world simulations; edge cases, unexpected inputs, adversarial conditions), monitoring aur feedback loops.

Costs: development costs (large datasets, specialized expertise, compute for training, iterative design/testing, data scientists/ML engineers/domain experts ki team, simulation environments/testing tools) aur operational costs (GPUs/cloud services, data storage/bandwidth, regular maintenance/updates). Optimization: lean models (rule-based system agar deep learning jaisa result de to simpler wala cost-effective hai), cloud-based resources (pay-as-you-go), open source models/tools. Cost ko value se justify karna padta hai: less critical tasks ke liye cheaper simpler agents, mission-critical ke liye heavy investment.

Example: large models high performance dete hain lekin expensive aur response delays la sakte hain; hybrid strategy me powerful model complex queries handle karta hai, lightweight model routine tasks — kuch systems me dynamic model routing har request ko complexity/urgency ke basis par appropriate model ko bhejta hai.

Table 2-1 (open-weight models, exact): Llama 3.1 Instruct Turbo (Meta, MMLU 56.1, 8B params, 20 GB VRAM, RTX 3090); Gemma 2 (Google, 72.1, 9B, 22.5 GB, RTX 3090); NeMo (Mistral, 65.3, 12B, 24 GB, RTX 3090); Phi-3 (Microsoft, 77.5, 14.7B, 29.4 GB, A100); Qwen1.5 (Alibaba, 74.4, 32B, 60.11 GB, A100); Llama 3 (Meta, 79.3, 70B, 160 GB, 4xA100). Book ka conclusion: larger models generally better perform karte hain, lekin inconsistently; ~14 billion parameters tak ke models single consumer-grade GPU (NVIDIA RTX 3090, 24 GB VRAM) par chal sakte hain; usse upar server-grade GPU (NVIDIA A100, 40 GB aur 80 GB varieties) chahiye. "Open weight" ka matlab: architecture aur weights (parameters) freely public ko release kiye gaye hain.

Table 2-2 (large models, exact MMLU): DeepSeek-v3 87.2; Claude 4 Opus Extended Thinking 86.5; Gemini 2.5 Pro 86.2; Llama 3.1 Instruct Turbo 405B 84.5; o4-mini 83.2; Nova Pro 82.0; Mistral Large 2 80.0; Grok 3 79.9. Prices Llama 3.1 ke price ke multiple me dikhaye gaye hain (publishing ke time least expensive tha: Meta charges $0.20 per million input tokens aur $0.60 per million output tokens). Book ka point: performance directly price se correlate nahi karti; benchmarks useful guidance dete hain lekin "your mileage may vary" — apne task par compare karke best price-per-performance wala model dhoondho.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaCore Components — Model, Tools, Memory, OrchestrationAgla →Single-Agent vs Multiagent Architecture
02.4Chapter 2 — Designing Agent Systems

Single-Agent vs Multiagent Architecture

Single-agent architecture me ek hi agent saare tasks manage/execute karta hai — environment se seedha interact karta hai, independently decision making, planning, execution karta hai, doosre agents par rely nahi karta. Multiagent me multiple agents common goal ke liye saath kaam karte hain — independently, parallel me, ya coordinated efforts se.

Single-agent kab best: well-defined, narrow tasks ke liye ideal hai — simple chatbots (FAQs, order tracking), task-specific automation (data entry, file management); design/develop/deploy easy hai kyunki coordination/communication/synchronization ki complexity nahi hai.

Multiagent ke advantages: collaboration and specialization (ek agent data collection, doosra processing, teesra user interactions — division of labour), parallelism (logistics me agents simultaneously different delivery routes plan karte hain), improved scalability (workload badhne par agents add karo), redundancy and resilience (ek agent fail ho to doosre continue karte hain ya uski responsibilities le lete hain).

Multiagent ki challenges: coordination and communication (information efficiently exchange karna, duplication/conflicting actions/resource contention avoid karna — bina proper orchestration ke disorganized/inefficient), increased complexity (communication protocols, coordination strategies, synchronization mechanisms), lower efficiency (aksar higher token consumption — agents ko frequently communicate, context share, coordinate karna padta hai, isse computational cost badhta hai aur task completion slow ho sakta hai).

Book ki discrepancy (honest note): text kehta hai "three common design patterns" lekin phir sirf do discuss karta hai — single-agent aur multiagent; teesra pattern naam se list nahi hota.

Kyun matter karta hai: architecture choice scalability, maintainability, flexibility ko influence karta hai. Multiagent complex, distributed, specialization wale environments ke liye suited hai (financial trading systems, cybersecurity investigations, collaborative AI research platforms); single-agent well-defined tasks ke liye. Book detail me Chapter 8 me discuss karega.

Example: logistics system me agents parallel me different delivery routes plan karke overall processing time ghata dete hain. Lekin multiagent me token consumption zyada hota hai kyunki agents ko baar-baar communicate aur context share karna padta hai — isiliye careful resource management crucial hai.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaDesign Trade-Offs — Speed, Scalability, Reliability, CostAgla →Best Practices — Iterative Design, Evaluation, Real-World Testing
02.5Chapter 2 — Designing Agent Systems

Best Practices — Iterative Design, Evaluation, Real-World Testing

Sirf sahi model/skills/architecture kaafi nahi — development lifecycle me teen best practices zaroori hain: iterative design (chhote functional prototypes banao, evaluate karo, refine karo), evaluation strategy (accuracy, efficiency, robustness, scalability par systematic testing), aur real-world testing (production environment me live users ke saath validate karo).

Iterative design: perfect solution pehli build me mat maango; core functionality pehle banao (MVP/basic agent), phir har iteration ke baad users/developers/stakeholders se feedback lo, aur refine karte raho; benefits: early detection of issues (design flaws/performance bottlenecks deeply embed hone se pehle pakdo), user-centric design (feedback se agent users ki needs/expectations se aligned rehta hai), scalability (manageable increments me grow karo, har addition thoroughly test karo).

Evaluation: functional testing (correctness; boundary testing — bahut bade datasets, unusual queries, ambiguous instructions jaise edge cases; task-specific metrics — legal/medical jaise domains ki accuracy/compliance requirements), generalization (training domain ke bahar naye tasks par adapt karna bina extensive retraining ke), user experience (NPS ya CSAT jaise satisfaction scores; task completion rates; explicit signals — thumbs-up/down, star ratings, accept/reject/modify; implicit signals — interaction logs mine karke misinterpretations, delays, sentiment, inappropriate responses pakdna), human-in-the-loop validation (human experts sample outputs review karein correctness/ethical compliance/best practices ke liye), end-to-end testing (data ingestion se task execution aur output generation tak, multiple systems/data sources/platforms across).

Real-world testing: phased rollout (chhote scale se start karke full deployment tak), monitor agent behaviour (KPIs: response time, accuracy, user satisfaction, system stability), user feedback collect karo, insights ke basis par iterate karo.

Kyun matter karta hai: controlled environment me agent predictable inputs par chalta hai; real world dynamic aur unpredictable hai — diverse users, edge cases, unforeseen challenges. Scripted queries par achha perform karne wala chatbot real users ke unexpected inputs, ambiguous questions, natural language variations par struggle kar sakta hai. Phased rollouts aur real-world testing hi promising prototypes ko reliable production systems me badalte hain.

Example: cancel-order agent ka minimal evaluation (code section me): tool sahi call hua? parameters sahi the (correct order ID)? confirmation message clear aur correct tha? Real evaluation isse deeper jaati hai — hundreds of examples par tool precision, parameter accuracy, overall task success rates measure karo taaki deploy se pehle edge cases pakde jaayein. Chapter 9 me evaluation strategies/frameworks depth me aayenge.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 2
← PichhlaSingle-Agent vs Multiagent ArchitectureAgla →Chapter 3 — User Experience
03Part 1 — Core Concepts

Chapter 3 — User Experience

UX hi decide karta hai ki agent effective, trustworthy, aur adopted hoga ya nahi — foundation models/architecture chahe kitne bhi remarkable hon. Is chapter me foundational design principles hain jo technologies badalne par bhi relevant rahein: interaction modalities, autonomy slider, synchronous vs asynchronous, context retention, aur trust.

Field unprecedented pace par evolve ho raha hai — naye interface paradigms, modality combinations, interaction models almost monthly emerge ho rahe hain — isiliye chapter technology-specific tricks ke bajaye principles deta hai.

Chapter ke conclusion ke 5 patterns yaad rakhna: communicate capabilities clearly (onboarding, suggestions, buttons); combine modalities thoughtfully (task/user context se align karo); retain context thoughtfully (relevant conversation state maintain karo bina memory overwhelm kiye ya privacy violate kiye); handle errors gracefully (clear polite fallbacks); build trust (limitations, confidence, reasoning ke baare me transparent raho).

Chapter ka core idea

"Context is UX" — agent cohesive, attentive collaborator lage ya disconnected tool jo user ko repeat karne par force kare, yehi decide karta hai. Aur: "Trust is gained in drops and lost in buckets."

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaBest Practices — Iterative Design, Evaluation, Real-World TestingAgla →Interaction Modalities — Text, GUI, Voice, Video
03.1Chapter 3 — User Experience

Interaction Modalities — Text, GUI, Voice, Video

Agents text, graphical interfaces, speech, aur video se interact kar sakte hain. Table 3-1 ke hisaab se: Text — very common (customer service chatbots, productivity assistants; ideal jab clear, asynchronous, ya searchable communication chahiye). Graphical user interfaces (GUI) — common (workflow orchestration dashboards, AI coding assistants like Cursor; ideal jab visual structure, context management, ya multistep workflows important hon). Speech/voice — less common (Siri, smart home assistants Alexa/Google Home, call center automation; ideal jab hands-free interaction ya natural conversation chahiye). Video — rare (virtual tutors, therapy avatars, interactive learning agents; ideal jab visual demonstration, rich expression, ya immersive learning chahiye).

Text-based interfaces simple, familiar, easy to integrate hain; synchronous aur asynchronous dono conversations support karte hain; clear traceable record banta hai (transparency, accountability, troubleshooting easy). AI terminals (Warp, Claude Code, Gemini CLI) ne text ko renaissance diya hai — natural language command translation, intelligent autocompletion, context-aware explanations; terminal ab conversational partner ban gaya hai. Text ka discoverability problem — user ko pata hi nahi hota agent kya-kya kar sakta hai ya command kaise phrase kare; GUI me buttons/menus visually batate hain, text me guess karna padta hai. Isiliye agent greeting ke saath capabilities bataye: sirf "How can I help you today?" nahi, balki "I can help you cancel orders, check delivery status, or update your account details."

GUI visual information present karke cognitive load ghata deta hai — progress bars, color coding, alert icons; tools jaise LangSmith, n8n, Arize, AutoGen workflows ko visually dikhane lage hain. Generative UIs dynamically interface elements/data visualizations/structured outputs create karte hain user query par (Perplexity AI structured knowledge cards, reference lists, data tables generate karta hai; AI coding copilots forms/config files/UI components generate karte hain).

Voice me latency historically major barrier thi, lekin past two years me low-latency speech recognition + efficient language processing ne delays dramatically ghata diye; interruptions, mid-sentence corrections, topic shifts handle karne lage hain. Voice ka speed math: humans typically 150–180 words per minute bolte hain, reading speed average 250–300 wpm hoti hai, skimming 500 wpm se zyada — isiliye dense/complex information ke liye spoken interfaces inherently slower hain; voice short, hands-free tasks ke liye best hai.

Video multiple sensory channels combine karta hai (visual cues, speech, text overlays, animations) — lekin uncanny valley, processing power/bandwidth, privacy concerns hain. Book kehta hai video interfaces "still in the uncanny valley" aur "getting closer to prime time"; fully conversational, multiturn, context-aware voice agents with action-taking capabilities "not yet widely deployed across industries".

Kyun matter karta hai: modality choice se user agent ko kaise perceive karta hai aur interact karta hai, woh shape hota hai. Koi single modality sab ke liye best nahi — task, environment, aur user expectations se align karni padti hai. Aur context management bhi UX hai: kuch apps me koi memory/learning nahi hoti (user ko information copy-paste karni padti hai); modern apps context automatically manage karte hain (Cursor IDE se intelligently code identify karke har inference me include karta hai); kuch long-term memory rakhte hain.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaChapter 3 — User ExperienceAgla →The Autonomy Slider — Manual / Ask / Agent
03.2Chapter 3 — User Experience

The Autonomy Slider — Manual / Ask / Agent

Effective agentic systems users ko agent ki autonomy smoothly adjust karne dete hain — fully manual control se partial automation se fully autonomous operation tak. Is concept ko autonomy slider kehte hain. Figure 3-4 iska simple example dikhata hai: "Manual", "Ask", ya "Agent" mode set karo, task/trust/context ke hisaab se.

Teen modes:

  • Manual: developer saara code khud likhta hai, IDE sirf editor hai (syntax highlighting, linting, no AI suggestions); customer support me human agents saari queries khud handle karte hain, AI inactive hai ya sirf backend analytics ke liye.
  • Ask (assisted): agent proactively code completions/refactors/documentation snippets suggest karta hai, lekin developer har suggestion review karke accept karta hai; support me agent suggested replies draft karta hai (recommended responses, policy references, troubleshooting steps), human review/edit/approve karke bhejta hai.
  • Agent: agent autonomously standard refactors apply karta hai, linter errors fix karta hai, project conventions par boilerplate code files generate karta hai bina individual approvals ke (developer ko changes notify kiye jaate hain); support me routine queries (password resets, order tracking, FAQs) bina human intervention ke handle karta hai, sirf complex/sensitive issues escalate karta hai.

Preferences static nahi hain — user trust, task familiarity, stakes, workload ke saath evolve hoti hain.

Kyun matter karta hai: autonomy slider sirf feature nahi hai — trust-building mechanism hai. Bina iske agents underpowered lagte hain (zyada manual input maangein to) ya overbearing (sensitive contexts me bina consent ke act karein to). Design principles: degrees of autonomy clearly expose karo (intuitive labels: "Manual", "Assist", "Auto", implications samjhao); seamless transitions enable karo (toggle/slider se review mode se auto-approve mode me quick shift); har level par predictable aur transparent behaviour do (partial automation me output draft karke explicit approval maango; full autonomy me bhi status updates aur intervene karne ke options do); har level ke risks/benefits communicate karo (critical tasks me full autonomy enable karne se pehle explicit confirmation maango); user trust aur competence ke basis par autonomy adapt karo (jaise 10 successful uses manual mode me, to assist mode try karne ka suggestion do).

Example: developer example (IDE) aur customer support example — dono me wahi teen modes coexist karte hain ek hi system me, aur team query complexity, customer profile, aur organizational trust ke basis par autonomy adjust kar sakti hai. Ye pattern kisi bhi field me extend ho sakta hai jahan workflows manual execution, AI assistance, aur full agentic automation ke beech fluidly shift karne se benefit karte hain.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaInteraction Modalities — Text, GUI, Voice, VideoAgla →Synchronous vs Asynchronous Experiences
03.3Chapter 3 — User Experience

Synchronous vs Asynchronous Experiences

Synchronous experiences me real-time back-and-forth hota hai (chat interfaces, voice conversations, real-time collaboration tools) — immediate responses chahiye. Asynchronous me agents aur users independently operate karte hain, communication intermittently hoti hai (email-like interactions, task notifications, process complete hone ke baad delivered reports).

Synchronous design principles: immediacy, clarity, responsiveness; low latency aur context awareness; clarity aur brevity (lambi explanations real-time rhythm tod deti hain); turn-taking mechanics (kab respond karna, kab wait karna, kab escalate karna); visual cues jaise typing indicators ya progress spinners reassure karte hain ki agent actively process kar raha hai; error handling — misunderstandings/failures se gracefully recover karo, uncertainty par clarifying questions poochho ya gently redirect karo, risky assumptions mat banao.

Asynchronous design principles: flexibility, persistence, clarity over time; task status/outcomes ki clear communication (user ko hamesha pata ho agent kya kar raha hai, task kis stage par hai, update kab expect karein); notifications, summaries, well-structured reports transparency maintain karte hain (analytical report generate karne wala agent bataye processing kab start hui, estimated completion time kya hai, aur finish par concise actionable summary deliver kare); context management critical hai (lambi delays ke baad bhi user ko information repeat nahi karni chahiye — Chapter 6 memory me detail); user expectations manage karo (clear timelines, progress indicators, follow-up notifications).

Dono useful aur valid patterns hain, lekin book highly recommend karta hai ki choose karo kaunsi experiences kis category me aati hain, taaki users pinwheel spin hote hue wait na karte rahein.

Proactivity ka balance sabse delicate hai — proactive alert urgent issue par immensely helpful ho sakta hai, lekin poorly timed notification high-stakes video meeting ke beech me disruptive ho sakti hai, ya completed task ki email notification perfectly appropriate ho sakti hai. Key hai context awareness aur user control: user ka current focus, urgency level, communication preferences samjho; relevance prioritize karo (notifications genuine value add karein, noise nahi); users ko notification frequency, channels, escalation thresholds par control do.

Example: voice assistant analytics report ka summary padhkar suna sakta hai, phir detailed text-based version charts ke saath email kar sakta hai later reference ke liye. User voice se driving ke waqt start karke, phone par text se meeting me jaate hue continue karke, laptop par graphical dashboard se results review kar sakta hai — modality fluidity ke liye state management aur context persistence zaroori hai taaki information/task progress/preferences transition me kabhi lost na hon.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaThe Autonomy Slider — Manual / Ask / AgentAgla →Context Retention, State, aur Personalization
03.4Chapter 3 — User Experience

Context Retention, State, aur Personalization

Context retention ka matlab hai agent multistep workflow, paused conversation, ya past interactions ke basis par apna behaviour adjust karte hue context maintain kare. Book kehta hai: "context is UX" — yehi decide karta hai ki agent cohesive, attentive collaborator lage ya disconnected tool jo user ko repeat karne par force kare.

State management context continuity ki foundation hai — agent ko accurately track karna hai kya hua, user kya achieve karna chahta hai, next logical step kya hai. Logged-in users ke liye state user account se tie hoti hai (devices/sessions across persistence); anonymous interactions ke liye session identifier (cookie ya token) chahiye. Scale par session state sirf memory me nahi rakhni chahiye — database ya distributed cache me persist karo (server restarts across continuity, load balancing, multidevice experiences).

User-based memory (persistent, personalized) vs session-based memory (ephemeral, session-scoped) ka choice privacy requirements, user expectations, operational architecture par depend karta hai. Short-term memory ongoing session ki details hold karti hai; long-term memory preferences/past interactions/broader patterns across sessions retain karti hai.

Implementation UX ko shape karta hai: purely client-side context (browser memory) session me fast hai lekin devices/logins across continuity kho deta hai; purely server-side context (user ID se tied database) long-term memory aur cross-device deta hai lekin latency ya privacy considerations la sakta hai; hybrid approach (short-term client par responsiveness ke liye, long-term server par continuity ke liye) aksar best UX balance deta hai.

Personalization teen forms me: preference retention (notification preferences, commonly chosen options yaad rakhna), behavioral adaptation (observed patterns par response style/interaction flow adjust karna), proactive assistance (past behaviour par user needs anticipate karke suggestions dena). Agar agent context bhool jaaye, to gracefully recover kare — clarifying questions poochhe, incorrect assumptions na banaye. State data securely manage karni hai, khaas taur par sensitive/personally identifiable information ho to.

Kyun matter karta hai: memory se continuity, personalization, intelligence ka sense banta hai. Lekin zyada context retain karna bhi problem hai — unwieldy ho sakta hai ya user privacy breach kar sakta hai. Best personalization invisible yet impactful hoti hai — agent subtly UX improve karta hai bina apne adjustments par attention draw kiye. Users ke paas hamesha personalized settings reset/override karne ka option hona chahiye.

Example: project management me agent user ki preferred task-tracking style recognize karke notifications/summaries adapt kar sakta hai. Customer service agent user ki preference ke hisaab se tone/verbosity adjust kar sakta hai — concise answers pasand hain ya detailed explanations. Travel booking, technical troubleshooting, ya multistep approval process me effective state management se interactions smooth, logical, productive rehti hain bina unnecessary repetition ke.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaSynchronous vs Asynchronous ExperiencesAgla →Trust — Capabilities, Confidence, Graceful Failure
03.5Chapter 3 — User Experience

Trust — Capabilities, Confidence, Graceful Failure

Book ka line: "Trust is gained in drops and lost in buckets." Trust ke liye transparency aur predictability do sabse powerful tools hain: users ko samajhna chahiye agent kya kar sakta hai, usne particular decision kyun liya, aur uski limitations kya hain.

Capabilities communicate karo — chat agents me input field ke neeche suggested action buttons ("Track order", "Generate summary", "Create meeting note"), onboarding tutorials/first-use walkthroughs, expandable menus/capability cards (sidebar me data retrieval, analysis, summarization, workflow automation), dynamic suggestions (user "book…" type kare to "Book meeting with [name]", "Book conference room", "Book travel" suggest karo). Open-ended text me agent khud conversation me capabilities bataye ("Hi, I can help you generate content, analyze data, or summarize documents. What would you like to do today?") aur capability ke bahar request par sirf reject na kare, alternatives de ("I can't process payments directly, but I can update your billing preferences or connect you with an agent who can assist."). Progressive disclosure use karo — pehle core capabilities, advanced features baad me; contextual relevance rakho.

Confidence/uncertainty communicate karo — explicit statements ("I'm 90% certain this is the correct answer."), visual cues (icons, color-coded alerts, confidence meters), behavioral adjustments (confidence low ho to firm recommendations ki jagah suggestions do). Overly confident mat bano jab uncertainty high ho — users jaldi trust kho dete hain agar agent confidently incorrect/misleading response de; lekin low-stakes me excessive hedging se agent hesitant/unreliable lagta hai.

Guidance maango — ambiguity par focused helpful questions poochho (user: "Book me a ticket to Chicago" → agent: "Would you like a one-way or round-trip ticket, and do you have preferred travel dates?"), kyun poochh rahe ho woh transparently batao ("I need a bit more information to proceed accurately"), ek saath bahut saare questions mat poochho, sabse critical ambiguities pehle solve karo, pehle di gayi information ko reference karo.

Gracefully fail karo — issue transparently acknowledge karo, helpful explanation do, actionable next steps suggest karo ("I couldn't find the information you're looking for; would you like me to escalate this to a human representative?"); predefined fallback mechanisms rakho (voice agent baar-baar samajh na paaye to text option par switch kare); multistep tasks me state preserve karo (user ko scratch se restart na karna pade); apologetic aur empathetic language use karo ("I'm sorry; something went wrong while processing your request. Let me try again or connect you with someone who can help."); failures se seekho (failure points log karo, recurring issues analyse karo, development process me feed karo).

Kyun matter karta hai: predictability ka matlab hai users prior interactions ke basis par anticipate kar sakein agent kaise respond karega. Erratic/inconsistent behaviour — technically correct bhi ho to — trust erode kar deta hai. Transparency ka matlab user ko reasoning ka har step dikhana nahi hai — bas enough insight taaki woh actions me confident feel kare, bina cognitive overload ke. Reliability: same question same conditions me same response; variability unavoidable ho (probabilistic LLM outputs) to clearly signal karo answer uncertain ya context-dependent hai; edge cases (incomplete data, conflicting instructions, ambiguous input) par predictably respond karo — clarifying questions, neutral fallback, ya escalation; system resilience (errors se recover karo, interruptions across state maintain karo, cascading failures prevent karo; external API connection kho jaaye to user ko notify karo, issue explain karo, sensible next step offer karo, silently fail mat karo ya misleading outputs mat do). Misaligned expectations (overpromise, underdeliver) limitations upfront admit karne se zyada trust damage karti hain.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 3
← PichhlaContext Retention, State, aur PersonalizationAgla →Chapter 4 — Tool Use
04Part 2 — Create, Orchestrate, Scale

Chapter 4 — Tool Use

Foundation models ghanton chat karne me great hain, lekin tools hi building blocks hain jo agents ko additional information/context retrieve karne, tasks perform karne, aur environment se meaningfully interact karne ki power dete hain.

Tool ki definition: ek specific capability ya set of actions jo agent desired outcome achieve karne ke liye perform kar sakta hai — simple single-step tasks se complex multistep operations tak. Agar agent se actual changes karwane hain, sirf search/provide information nahi, to tools hi woh changes execute karenge.

Chapter LangChain ke fundamentals se start karta hai, phir tool types cover karta hai sequence me: local tools, API-based tools, plug-in tools, Model Context Protocol (MCP), stateful tools, aur automated tool development (foundation models as tool makers, real-time code generation, tool use configuration).

Chapter ka core idea

Building and maintaining the toolkit for your agent is one of the most critical ways to give your agent the capabilities to succeed. Aur: sirf woh tools bind karo jinhe model aise execute kare ki good harm se zyada ho — ye developers ki paramount responsibilities me se ek hai.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaTrust — Capabilities, Confidence, Graceful FailureAgla →LangChain Fundamentals
04.1Chapter 4 — Tool Use

LangChain Fundamentals

LangChain ke heart me foundation models aur chat models hain jo prompts process karke responses generate karte hain. ChatOpenAI ek wrapper class hai jo OpenAI ke chat-based models (jaise GPT-5) se interact karne ka simple interface deta hai — model name jaise parameters se initialize karte hain.

Messages: interactions messages ke roop me structure hoti hain conversational context maintain karne ke liye — HumanMessage (user inputs) aur AIMessage (model responses). Tools external functions hain jinhe model text generation se aage capabilities extend karne ke liye call kar sakta hai — APIs call karna, database entries retrieve karna, calculations perform karna.

Basic loop (4 building blocks):

  • @tool decorator se tool define karo — ye function register karta hai aur automatically schema generate karta hai jo uske inputs/outputs describe karta hai.
  • .bind_tools() se tools ko model se bind karo — isse model user inputs ke response me tools select aur invoke kar sakta hai.
  • .invoke() se model se interact karo, current conversation ko represent karne wale messages ki list dekar.
  • Agar model tool call karne ka decide kare, to woh tool call output karega; tum corresponding function execute karo aur uska result conversation me waapas append karo, phir final response generate karo.

Example (code section me): llm = ChatOpenAI(model_name="gpt-4o"); messages = [HumanMessage("What is the weather today?")]; @tool def add_numbers(x: int, y: int) -> int: """Adds two numbers and returns the sum.""" return x + y; llm_with_tools = llm.bind_tools([add_numbers]); ai_msg = llm_with_tools.invoke(messages); phir for tool_call in ai_msg.tool_calls: tool_response = add_numbers.invoke(tool_call).

Kyun matter karta hai: ye chaar building blocks — chat models, messages, tools, tool invocation — LangChain-based systems ki foundation hain. Inhe samajhne se chapter ke examples follow karna aur apne agents banana easy ho jaata hai jo language understanding ko real-world actions se seamlessly integrate karte hain.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaChapter 4 — Tool UseAgla →Local Tools
04.2Chapter 4 — Tool Use

Local Tools

Local tools locally run karne ke liye design kiye jaate hain — predefined rules/logic par based, specific tasks ke liye tailored, agent ke saath co-deploy hote hain. Ye khaas taur par language models ki weaknesses ko augment karte hain jahan traditional programming better perform karta hai: arithmetic, time-zone conversions, calendar operations, maps ke saath interactions.

Metadata hi sab kuch hai: tool ka metadata — naam, description, schema — uski logic jitna hi critical hai, kyunki model usi metadata se decide karta hai kaunsa tool invoke karna hai. Isiliye: precise, narrowly scoped names chuno (naam zyada general ho to LLM use bula lega jab zaroorat nahi hai); clear, distinctive descriptions likho (overly broad ya overlapping descriptions multiple tools me confusion aur poor performance guarantee karte hain); strict input/output schemas define karo (explicit schemas se foundation model ko exactly samajh aata hai tool kab aur kaise use karna hai, misfires ghate hain).

Calculator example (code section me): multiply, exponentiate, add define karo, llm.bind_tools(tools) se bind karo, phir query "What is 393 * 12.25? Also, what is 11 + 49?" par model do function calls invoke karta hai — multiply {'x': 393, 'y': 12.25} Result: 4814.25 aur add {'x': 11, 'y': 49} 60.0 — aur final response hota hai "393 times 12.25 is 4814.25, and 11 + 49 is 60."

Fayde: local tools precision, predictability, simplicity dete hain — logic explicitly define hoti hai isiliye predictable aur reliable hote hain.

Drawbacks: scalability (design/build/deploy cumbersome, time-consuming, challenging; share karna across use cases mushkil), duplication (har team/deployment ko wahi library deploy karni padegi, changes push karne ke liye har agent service se coordination chahiye — practice me bahut si teams coordination overhead avoid karne ke liye same tools independently reimplement kar leti hain), maintenance (environment/requirements badalne par handcrafted tools ko frequent updates chahiye, ongoing maintenance resource-intensive hai aur typically agent service ki redeployment chahiye hoti hai).

Example: simple mathematical operations best example hain — unit conversions, calculator operations, calendar changes, dates/times par operations, maps/graphs par operations — in sab me handcrafted tools agentic systems ki efficacy substantially improve kar sakte hain.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaLangChain FundamentalsAgla →API-Based Tools
04.3Chapter 4 — Tool Use

API-Based Tools

API-based tools agents ko external services se interact karne dete hain — additional information access karna, data process karna, actions execute karna jo locally feasible nahi hain. APIs se public/private services se communicate karke agent ki functionality dynamic aur scalable tareeke se extend hoti hai.

Benefits: range of tasks dramatically expand hoti hai (weather API se current conditions/forecasts, financial API se stock prices, translation API se multilingual support — bina model retrain kiye); real-time data access (latest information par based responses/actions — financial trading ya emergency response me crucial jahan decisions latest data par quickly lene hote hain).

Wikipedia example (code section me): WikipediaAPIWrapper(top_k_results=1, doc_content_chars_max=300) aur WikipediaQueryRun se tool register karo, ChatOpenAI(model_name="gpt-4o", temperature=0) se bind karo, query "What was the most impressive thing about [Name]?" par model Wikipedia search karta hai aur additional information se final answer generate karta hai. top_k_results=1 matlab sirf top 1 result, doc_content_chars_max=300 matlab max 300 characters content.

Stock example (code section me): @tool def get_stock_price(ticker: str) -> float — api_url = f"https://api.example.com/stocks/{ticker}", requests.get, status 200 ho to data["price"] return karo, warna ValueError raise karo; query "What is the stock price of Apple?" par model tool call karta hai. Note: api.example.com ek example/placeholder URL hai, real stock API nahi hai.

Design karte waqt focus karo reliability, security, graceful failure par: external services down ho sakti hain isiliye fallbacks ya clear error messages chahiye; saari communications HTTPS aur strong authentication se secure karo, khaas taur par sensitive data ke liye; API rate limits ka dhyaan rakho; data privacy laws ka compliance rakho (zaroorat ho to user data anonymize/obfuscate karo); errors robustly handle karo taaki agent network issues ya invalid responses se recover kar sake bina user experience tode; jab possible ho, alternatives/multiple providers consider karo taaki koi ek provider degrade ho to reliability bani rahe.

Kyun matter karta hai: APIs agents ko real-time data, heavy computation, aur external actions dete hain jo woh akele perform nahi kar sakte — isse woh far more capable aur effective ban jaate hain. Team/company-specific information par bhi similar tools bana kar tasks ka scope aur complexity significantly expand ki ja sakti hai.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaLocal ToolsAgla →MCP — USB-C Port for AI
04.4Chapter 4 — Tool Use

MCP — USB-C Port for AI

Model Context Protocol (MCP) ek open standard hai jo Anthropic ne introduce kiya tha (aur tab se OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Microsoft jaise major players ne adopt kar liya hai) — LLMs ko external systems se connect karne ka uniform, model-agnostic tareeka. Book isey "USB-C port for AI" kehta hai: ek single, well-defined interface jo koi bhi data source ya tool expose kar sakta hai, aur koi bhi agent consume kar sakta hai, bina specialized glue code ke.

Do roles hain:

  • MCP server: ek web server jo standardized JSON-RPC 2.0 interface se data/services expose karta hai; server kuch bhi wrap kar sakta hai — cloud object storage, SQL databases, enterprise CRM, proprietary business logic — bas MCP specification implement karni hai.
  • MCP client: koi bhi agent ya LLM application jo MCP "bolta" hai; client JSON-RPC requests bhejta hai (e.g. "List all files in this Salesforce folder" ya "Execute function 'getCustomerBalance' with customerId=1234") aur structured JSON responses receive karta hai.

Kaise kaam karta hai: under the hood MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 use karta hai over HTTPS ya WebSocket. Servers apne available methods advertise karte hain (e.g. listFiles, getRecord, runAnalysis) aur unke input/output schemas; clients server ka "method catalog" fetch karte hain, jisse LLM reason kar sakta hai kaunsa method call karna hai aur kin parameters ke saath; phir MCP client us call ko JSON-RPC payload me wrap karke appropriate server ko bhejta hai aur response ka wait karta hai.

Example (code section me): local "math" MCP server subprocess se launch karo, remote "weather" MCP server localhost:8000/mcp se connect karo, async agent loop last message inspect karke decide karta hai "math" tool call karna hai (arithmetic expressions ke liye) ya "weather" tool (weather queries ke liye) — simple heuristic: digit-operator tokens (+, -, *, /, (, )) hon to "math", "weather" word ho to "weather", warna direct reply "Sorry, I can only answer math or weather queries."

Kyun matter karta hai: MCP se pehle developers har target system ke liye custom adapters likhte the — REST calls ya SDK usage seedha agent code me hard-code karte the; data sources badhne par bespoke integrations multiply ho jaati thi, brittle, error-prone code banta tha jo maintain/extend karna mushkil tha. MCP ke baad ek baar service MCP se expose kar do, to kitne bhi agents uske methods discover aur invoke kar sakte hain bina har agent ke liye custom adapters rewrite kiye — development effort dramatically ghata deta hai aur modular, reusable architectures encourage karta hai. Platforms jaise Glama.ai aur mcp.so large numbers of MCP servers aggregate karte hain, searchable/discoverable banate hain — simple utilities se complex stateful services tak.

Lekin security abhi unresolved hai — book saaf kehta hai: authentication, access controls, aur potential attack vectors (jab multiple agents MCP endpoints share karte hain) par security issues raise hue hain aur fully addressed nahi hain; sirf authorized agents hi specific methods invoke karein, sensitive data par role-based access control ho, malicious payload injection prevent ho, audit logs maintain hon — ye active research/engineering areas hain; core MCP specification abhi tak ek single standardized security solution mandate nahi karti; kuch organizations additional network policies ya proxy layers se mitigate karte hain.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaAPI-Based ToolsAgla →Plug-In, Stateful Tools aur Automated Tool Development
04.5Chapter 4 — Tool Use

Plug-In, Stateful Tools aur Automated Tool Development

Plug-in tools modular hote hain, minimal customization se agent ke framework me integrate ho jaate hain, existing libraries/APIs/third-party services leverage karte hain — rapid deployment aur scaling enable karte hain. Stateful tools local scripts, external APIs, aur MCP-deployed services across span karte hain, lekin unka common risk hai: foundation model ko persistent state par direct power de do, to woh destructive mistakes kar sakta hai ya bad actors exploit kar sakte hain. Automated tool development me AI agents autonomously code likhte hain (code generation), jisse software applications create/maintain karne ka time/effort significantly ghata jaata hai.

Plug-in tools — platform-wise: OpenAI ke plug-ins ecosystem me powerful extensions hain (real-time web search se specialized code generators tak), lekin woh sirf ChatGPT product ke andar available hain, public API me nahi — Expedia, Zapier, ya koi first-party ChatGPT plug-in standard OpenAI Completions/Chat endpoints se invoke nahi kar sakte; replicate karne ke liye custom function-calling layers (e.g. LangChain se) banana padte hain. Anthropic's Claude apni full "tool use" capability seedha Anthropic Messages API se expose karta hai (aur Amazon Bedrock ya Google Cloud Vertex AI par) — custom tools register karo (ya Anthropic-provided use karo), Claude inference time par call kar sakta hai, no separate UI. Google's Gemini Vertex AI API se function calling support karta hai — tools FunctionCallingConfig me declare karo, Gemini unhe structured calls ke roop me invoke karta hai. Microsoft's Phi models Azure AI Foundry se offer hote hain, Azure services (cognitive search, document processing, data visualization APIs) se seamlessly integrate hote hain. Open source me Hugging Face Transformers library pretrained models aur plug-in tools deti hai NLP tasks ke liye.

Plug-in tools ki limit: model execution layer par integration easy hai, lekin custom-developed tools jitni customizability/adaptability nahi dete — general-purpose hote hain, har application ki specific needs ke liye tailored nahi hote. Plug-in catalogs leading platforms ke rapidly grow ho rahe hain, aur interoperability/standardization future focus hai.

Stateful tools — principle of least power: book ka real-world case — ek AI agent ne database performance "optimize" karte hue production table ki aadhi rows drop kar di, critical records erase ho gaye. Mitigation: sirf narrowly scoped operations register karo, "execute arbitrary SQL" endpoint expose mat karo — jaise get_user_profile(user_id) ya add_new_customer(record) tools, har ek single well-tested query/procedure encapsulate karta hai; sirf read access chahiye wale agents ko kabhi delete/modify rights mat do; free-form queries absolutely demand karein to rigorous sanitization aur access controls implement karo — OWASP's GenAI Security Project warn karta hai ki prompt injections dangerous clauses jaise DROP ya ALTER benign requests me slip kara sakte hain, isiliye input validation aise statements reject kare; hamesha parameters bind karo ya prepared statements use karo SQL injection prevent karne ke liye; database account ke paas sirf minimum privileges hon; har tool invocation log karo anomalous behaviour detect karne aur forensic analysis ke liye, aur suspicious patterns (unusually large deletions, schema-altering commands) par real-time alerts rakho. Principle: least power — model ko sirf woh tools do jo use strictly chahiye, aur har operation ko precise boundaries aur oversight se guard karo.

Foundation Models as Tool Makers: foundation models ab sirf tools consume nahi karte, banate bhi hain — LLM ko API specifications ya sample inputs do, woh initial wrappers/helper functions/higher-level "atomic" operations generate karega; model ko code stubs draft karne do, safe sandbox me execute karo, phir apna output khud critique karne do ("That endpoint returned a 400—adjust the query parameters."). Kuch rapid iterations me well-tested, narrowly scoped tools ka suite mil jaata hai bina har wrapper haath se craft kiye. Sprawling API landscape me model ko OpenAPI spec (ya code samples) par point karo, har function ka first draft spin up karne do; human reviewers phir generated code validate aur tighten karte hain CI/CD pipeline me jaane se pehle. As APIs evolve, rerun the same generate-and-refine loop to keep tools in sync — saving weeks of boilerplate work. Lekin clear validation criteria (tests, response checks, schema enforcement) aur developer oversight demand karta hai — edge cases pakdna, security gaps guard karna, business logic alignment confirm karna ultimately tumhari responsibility hai.

Real-Time Code Generation: AI agent operation ke dauraan zaroorat padne par code likhta aur execute karta hai — naye tools create karna ya existing modify karna, novel API ya unfamiliar problem par. Process: task analyse karo → code snippets likho → execute karo → fail ho to iteratively revise karo, har attempt se seekhte hue. Advantages: adaptability aur efficiency (real-time data analysis, complex software integration). Risks: quality control (poor-quality code → system failures, security breaches), security (self-generated code execute karne se malicious actors harmful code inject kar sakte hain), repeatability (har baar scratch se recreate karne par predictability khatam — ek invocation ki success agli ki guarantee nahi; prompts ya model updates se bilkul alag code paths), resource consumption (naive solutions draft/execute karna compute/memory heavy). Guardrails on multiple aspects of system performance se mitigate karo.

Tool Use Configuration: foundation model APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, aur zyada) tool-choice parameter se model ke tool use ko explicitly control karne dete hain — flexible foundation model-driven invocation se deterministic behavior tak. "auto" mode me model context ke basis par decide karta hai tools call karne hain ya nahi (general use ke liye achha). "any"/"required" model ko force karta hai kam se kam ek tool invoke kare (ideal jab tool output essential ho). "none" saare tool calls block kar deta hai (controlled outputs ya testing environments ke liye useful). Kuch interfaces specific tool pin karne bhi dete hain, predictable repeatable flows ke liye. Sahi mode chunna flexibility, reliability, aur predictability ka balance hai.

Fallback aur postprocessing: best agents bhi misstep kar sakte hain — necessary tool calls skip karna, invalid JSON output karna, ya error karne wale tools chalana — isliye reliable fallback mechanisms chahiye. Har model response ke baad inspect karo: sahi tools invoke hue? valid JSON aaya? runtime errors ke bina succeed hua? Agar kuch toota, to corrective flow: validate first using your schema (e.g. jsonschema ya Pydantic) — missing fields ya malformed structures pakdo; tool skip hua to automatically trigger karo; JSON invalid ho to model ko correct karne ko kaho. Retry intelligently — exponential backoff for transient failures, ya sirf problematic portion regenerate karo poora exchange restart karne ke bajaye. Fall back gracefully jab retries fail hon — backup model/service par switch karo, user se clarification maango, cached data use karo, ya safe default return karo. Log everything — prompts, tool calls, validation errors, retries, fallbacks — observability, debugging, aur continuous improvement ke liye.

Chapter ka conclusion: tools enable AI agents to perform tasks, make decisions, aur interact with their environment effectively. Handcrafted tools precision dete hain lekin maintain karna time-consuming hai. Plug-in tools rapid integration aur scalability dete hain lekin customizability kam hai. Automated tool development (real-time code generation, imitation learning, reinforcement learning) agents ko dynamically adapt aur refine karne deta hai — versatility aur problem-solving badhta hai, continuous improvement aur autonomous expansion of tools possible hoti hai.

Examples: plug-in tools customer support (queries handle karna, solutions dena, tickets manage karna), healthcare (medical image analysis, patient triage, data management), finance (market trends analyse karna, fraud detect karna, portfolios manage karna), education (personalized learning, automated grading, content recommendation) me use hote hain.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 4
← PichhlaMCP — USB-C Port for AIAgla →Chapter 5 — Orchestration
05Part 2 — Create, Orchestrate, Scale

Chapter 5 — Orchestration

Orchestration woh core logic hai jo user ki query ko lekar decide karta hai — kaunsa tool chalana hai, kaise chalana hai, aur jawab kaise banana hai. Book kehta hai: orchestration ki success hi agent ki success decide karti hai.

Is chapter me 3 bade topics hain: (1) agent types — Reflex, ReAct, Planner-Executor, Query-Decomposition, Reflection, Deep Research; (2) tool selection — Standard, Semantic, Hierarchical; aur (3) tool execution aur topologies — Single, Parallel, Chains, Graphs. Aakhir me context engineering — prompt engineering se aage ka kaam.

Book ki 5 best practices yaad rakhna: (1) latency vs accuracy ka trade-off hamesha socho; (2) typical number of actions dekho — zyada actions matlab zyada complex planning; (3) plan ko results ke hisaab se kitna badalna padega, woh assess karo; (4) alag planning approaches ko evaluate karne ke liye representative test cases banao; (5) simplest approach chuno jo requirements poori kare — chhote se shuru karo, complexity sirf tab badhao jab use case maange.

Chapter ka core idea

Orchestration = reasoning + tool selection + execution + planning, sahi order me, sahi cost par. Galat orchestration chuni to agent ya to slow/mahanga hoga, ya complex kaam handle nahi kar payega.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaPlug-In, Stateful Tools aur Automated Tool DevelopmentAgla →Agent Types — 6 Kismein
05.1Chapter 5 — Orchestration

Agent Types — 6 Kismein

Agent type matlab agent ka reasoning, planning aur action karne ka tareeka. Book 6 archetypes deta hai — aur saaf kehta hai ki ye starting point hai, definitive taxonomy nahi; field bahut tezi se badal raha hai, hybrid patterns aate rahenge.

  • Reflex: seedha input → action mapping, bina soche. "If X, to tool Y chalao" — keyword-based routing ya single-step data lookup ke liye kaafi hai.
  • ReAct: socho → tool chalao → result dekho → dobara socho, loop me. Dynamic kaam ke liye best.
  • Planner-Executor: pehle poora plan banao, phir step-by-step execute karo. Planning aur execution alag phases.
  • Query-Decomposition: bade sawaal ko chhote sawaalon me todo, har ek ke liye search karo, phir final answer jodo.
  • Reflection: ReAct + apne past steps ko review karke galti sudhaaro.
  • Deep Research: planner + decomposition + ReAct + reflection, sab combine karke lambe investigation karo — literature review ya market analysis jaise open-ended kaam ke liye.

Kyun matter karta hai: agent type seedha performance, cost aur latency ko affect karta hai. Galat type chuna to ya to bahut slow/mahanga system banega, ya complex kaam handle nahi hoga. Simple kaam ke liye Reflex kaafi hai; open-ended investigation ke liye Deep Research chahiye.

Example: keyword-based routing ya single-step data lookup ke liye Reflex agent kaafi hai; literature review jaise kaam ke liye Deep Research agent chahiye jo plan → decompose → search → reflect → synthesize karta hai.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaChapter 5 — OrchestrationAgla →ReAct aur Planner-Executor
05.2Chapter 5 — Orchestration

ReAct aur Planner-Executor

ReAct (Reasoning + Action) me model thought likhta hai, tool call karta hai, observation dekhta hai, aur zaroorat padne par repeat karta hai. Planner-Executor me planning aur execution alag phases hain — pehle plan, phir execute.

ReAct kaise kaam karta hai: LangChain ke variants — ZERO_SHOT_REACT_DESCRIPTION (saare tools + instructions ek hi prompt me, bina example traces ke) aur CHAT_ZERO_SHOT_REACT_DESCRIPTION (isme conversational history bhi hoti hai). ReAct exploratory kaam — dynamic data analysis, multisource aggregation, troubleshooting — me best hai kyunki mid-stream adapt kar sakta hai. Uska chain-of-thought debugging aur audit me bhi madad karta hai, lekin latency aur API cost badhta hai.

Planner-Executor kaise kaam karta hai: planner bada model ho sakta hai aur executor chhote model ya kam LLM calls se kaam chala sakta hai — cost efficiency ka fayda. Explicit plan hone se debugging aasan hai — plan dekho, kaunsa step fail hua track karo, replan karo.

Query-Decomposition example (SELF_ASK_WITH_SEARCH): "Who lived longer, X or Y?" → self-ask "What's X's lifespan?" → search → self-ask "What's Y's lifespan?" → search → synthesize "X lived 85 years, Y lived 90 years, so Y lived longer". Har fact tool output se grounded hota hai, phir final answer banta hai.

Kab kaunsa: dynamic, unpredictable kaam ke liye ReAct; jab plan pehle se clear ho aur cost bachani ho, to Planner-Executor.

SOURCESource: Building Applications with AI Agents, O'Reilly, Chapter 5
← PichhlaAgent Types — 6 KismeinAgla →Tool Selection — Standard, Semantic, Hierarchical
05.3Chapter 5 — Orchestration

Tool Selection — Standard, Semantic, Hierarchical

Tool selection matlab user query ke liye sahi tool chunna. Book 3 strategies deta hai:

  • Standard: saare tool definitions model ko do, model chune. Simple hai, lekin bahut saare tools par scale nahi karta, aur har baar ek extra foundation-model call se latency badhti hai (seconds add ho sakte hain).
  • Semantic: tool descriptions ko embed karke vector search se top tools nikalo, phir model chune. Sabse common pattern hai aur book ise most use cases ke liye recommend karta hai — fast, performant, reasonably scalable. Lekin semantic collisions ki wajah se selection accuracy aksar worse hoti hai (similar descriptions wale tools ke embeddings paas aa jate hain).
  • Hierarchical: pehle tool GROUP chuno (Computation, Automation, Communication), phir us group ke andar tool chuno. Accuracy badhata hai, lekin slow hai kyunki multiple sequential foundation-model calls lagte hain, aur groups banana/maintain karna mehnat ka kaam hai — sirf tab use karo jab tools bahut zyada hon.

Semantic kaise kaam karta hai: pehle se har tool description ko encoder-only model (OpenAI Ada, Amazon Titan, Cohere Embed, ModernBERT) se vector banakar lightweight vector DB (jaise FAISS) me store karte hain; runtime par query embed karke top tools retrieve karte hain.
